chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the woman who sees blood before her regular time of menstruation. So he said: When she sees blood before her regular time of menstruation, let her abandon salat, for perhaps the time has come early for her. So if it is more than her days in which she used to menstruate, let her wait three days after her days have passed. Then if she has waited three days and the blood has not stopped from her, let her do as the woman with istihadha does.

key_terms.إِسْتِحَاضَة: Istihadha - irregular/inter-period bleeding; a distinct legal category with different rulings from haydh
key_terms.الصَّلَاة: Salat - the obligatory ritual prayer, which is suspended during haydh
key_terms.حَيْض: Haydh - menstruation; the regular monthly bleeding with specific jurisprudential rulings

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she sees blood before her regular menstruation time according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the jurisprudential ruling for a woman who experiences bleeding before her expected menstrual period. The Imam rules that she should immediately abandon prayer (treating it as haydh), but if the bleeding extends beyond her regular cycle, she should wait three additional days before applying the rulings of istihadha (irregular/continuous bleeding). This ruling reflects the Imami jurisprudential principle of precaution when uncertain about the nature of bleeding.
